To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

TAK1 is expressed in endothelial cells in the blood-brain barrier, that it is required for the production of fever and sickness behaviors in response to peripheral inflammatory stimuli, and that it does so by regulating the production of prostaglanins.
TAK1 in the brain endothelium is required for production of prostacyclin (a prostaglandin) in the endothelium and fever in response to inflammation.
TAK1 expression in the brain is necessary for the production of prostagandins and cytokines in the brain, and is necessary for the induction of fever and lethargic behavior.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of fever, and the role of fever in the immune response to pathogens.
the role of the TAK1 signaling pathway in the regulation of the immune response.
understanding the molecular and cellular events that occur in the brain during the acute phase of inflammation, with a particular focus on the role of endothelial cells in the brain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the expression of TAK1 in endothelial cells of the blood-brain barrier (BBB) is necessary for the induction of fever and the sickness behaviour.
TAK1 is a key molecule for the induction of fever and lethargicity in response to peripheral immune challenge.
TAK1 is required in brain endothelial cell to mediate fever and sickness behavior in response to systemic LPS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TAK1 in endothelial cells is a key regulator of the neurovascular unit, a structure that is critical for the integration of brain function with peripheral physiology.
we found a new role for brain endothelial cells as a source for the inflammatory signal PGE2.
TAK1 in endothelial cells mediats the production of prostagladin E2, which is needed for fever and sickness behavior.
The main takeaway from our work is that
endothelial cells are not just passive conduits for molecules and cells, but are active players in the immune response, and in the response to inflammation, in the brain.
the brain endothelium is a key mediator of sickness behavior.
the brain endothelium is an active participant in the neuroinflammation that accompanies systemic inflammation, and that it is a key regulator of the behavioral changes that accompany inflammation.
